entry.title: Difference Between UI and UX — Simple Explanation
entry.summary: When we talk about UI and UX, people often confuse them, but they are very different: Focuses on how a product feels. Concerned with the user journey, usability, and overall experience. Example: How easy is it to navigate an app? Does the workflow make sense? Focuses on how a product looks. Concerned with visual elements like buttons, colors, typography, and layout. Example: The style of the buttons, the color scheme, and the placement of elements. Think of a car: UX = How comfortable and smooth the ride is. UI = How the dashboard, steering wheel, and controls look. Key takeaway: UX is about experience, UI is about appearance. Both work together to make a product user-friendly and visually appealing.
